sourceFitAssessment.learnerTask: See why the same binding module changes its contact and signaling context in a soluble format versus a membrane CAR.
sourceFitAssessment.gap: The format table names differences but leaves contact geometry and antigen-independent clustering entirely verbal.
sourceFitAssessment.accuracyGuardrails: Keep the same recognition module while changing format, geometry and signaling context. Do not infer that one architecture or affinity is universally safer, more active or more effective.
sourceFitAssessment.reasoning: The teal recognition shape and orange target remain consistent across a soluble assembly and a membrane CAR. The soluble scene has one target membrane and no intracellular receptor signal tail; the CAR scene has two opposing surfaces and a continuous binder-to-spacer-to-membrane-to-internal-tail connection. The body explains the spacer and identifies signaling as intracellular. This is a schematic format contrast, not an intact IgG/domain architecture claim or architectural ranking. Product-specific stability, expression, contact geometry and clustering tests remain separate, and affinity alone does not establish safety or activity.
